properties.statement: THE UNDECLARED-SEAM FINDING COULD NOT REACH ZERO, AND THE REASON WAS AN ALTITUDE MISMATCH RATHER THAN MISSING CONTRACTS. `fact:coupling-and-contract-are-recorded-in-vocabularies-that-never-meet` measured the two sets as DISJOINT BY CONSTRUCTION — couplings read from DEPENDS_ON between modules, contracts from PROVIDES/CONSUMES between the boxes that contain them — so writing a contract could never move the number. MEASURED 2026-08-23 on reflow2's own design: module level 72 couplings against 42 contract pairs leaves 64 undeclared; LIFTED TO `subsystem` it is 11 against 13 with NOTHING undeclared. || ⭐ LIFTING BOTH SETS IS THE WHOLE CORRECTNESS ARGUMENT, AND THE HALF-FIX LOOKS RIGHT. Rolling up only the COUPLINGS is the obvious move and leaves the two vocabularies exactly as disjoint as they were — the contracts are still recorded between the leaves. Proven by reverting to that half-fix and watching the one case that matters fail while four others stayed green, which is why the case exists. || ⚠️ A ZERO HERE IS THE MOST DANGEROUS ANSWER THE TOOL CAN GIVE, and it is designed around. 'Nothing undeclared' at subsystem altitude compared ELEVEN couplings, not seventy-two. Every reply therefore carries the raw count and, when an altitude reaches nothing, the number of endpoints dropped — asked at `system`, where this design has no components at all, it reports 0 couplings compared and 114 endpoints unreachable rather than a clean bill. A vacuous zero that announces its own vacuity. || NOTHING IS WRITTEN BACK. The roll-up is derived on every call from CONTAINS + PROVIDES + CONSUMES. A stored edge between two subsystems would make the graph assert a contract nobody declared and be indistinguishable afterwards from one somebody did — `dec:views-are-projections`, and Anthony's own standing rule that a view is a projection and renderer fill-ins are defects. Pinned by a case that exports the design before and after and compares content hashes. || WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE: whether `detect_undeclared_seams` and the maturity `seams` band should themselves move to an altitude, or keep answering at module level. They are unchanged here on purpose — changing what a detector reports is a louder act than adding a way to ask, and the 64 remains visible until somebody decides which altitude that gap is about. || SOURCE: measured 2026-08-23 on reflow2 0.38.0, driving the built binary over real stdio.
